forms.difference: Form I perfect; it states a completed act of sacrificing, slaughtering or striking at the throat, while the current occurrence is an imperative command.
forms.relationship: Form I perfect of the ن ح ر root; it is the completed-action counterpart of the current imperative ٱنْحَرْ.
forms.provenance: Codex-authored after review of the approved project root meaning, the Arabic Academy lexicon entry for نَحَرَ and standard Arabic Form I morphology.

forms.difference: Form I imperfect, third-person masculine singular; it presents sacrificing or slaughtering as ongoing or habitual.
forms.relationship: Form I imperfect of the ن ح ر root; it is the ongoing counterpart of نَحَرَ and the indicative counterpart of the command.
forms.provenance: Codex-authored after review of the approved project root meaning, the Arabic Academy lexicon entry for نَحَرَ and standard Arabic Form I imperfect morphology.

forms.difference: Verbal noun; it names the act of sacrificing or slaughtering rather than expressing it as a finite verb.
forms.relationship: A genuine verbal noun of the ن ح ر root, naming the action expressed by نَحَرَ and ٱنْحَرْ.
forms.provenance: Codex-authored after review of the approved project root meaning, the Arabic Academy lexicon entry for نَحَرَ and standard Arabic Form I verbal-noun morphology.

forms.difference: Form II perfect; the doubled middle radical marks an intensified or repeated slaughtering action.
forms.relationship: A genuine Form II verb of the ن ح ر root; the Arabic Academy lexicon defines نَحَّرَ الإبلَ as slaughtering many camels or similar animals.
forms.provenance: Codex-authored after review of the Arabic Academy lexicon entry for نَحَّرَ and standard Arabic Form II morphology.

forms.difference: Form I perfect; it states a completed act or settled attitude of hating, while the current occurrence is the active participle naming the hater.

forms.difference: Form I imperfect, third-person masculine singular; it presents hatred as ongoing or habitual rather than naming the hater as a noun.

forms.difference: Verbal noun; it names the hostility itself rather than the person who hates, and it is the Qur'anic form seen in 5:2 and 5:8.
forms.relationship: A genuine verbal noun of the ش ن أ root, attested in the Qur'an as شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ and semantically connected to شَانِئَكَ.
forms.provenance: Codex-authored after review of canonical Qur'anic occurrences 5:2 and 5:8, the Quranic Arabic Corpus root entry for ش ن أ and reliable Arabic lexicon evidence.

forms.difference: Passive participle; it describes someone or something that is hated, contrasting the object of hatred with the active hater in شَانِئَكَ.
forms.relationship: A genuine passive-participle form of the ش ن أ root, recorded in Arabic lexicon evidence as مَشْنُوءٌ.
forms.provenance: Codex-authored after review of Lane's Lexicon and classical Arabic lexicon evidence for مَشْنُوءٌ, alongside the approved project root meaning.
